card.band: 8 h. Many levers (similarity, shrinkage, iALS, recency, ensembling), so partial credit is dense. Frontier agents beat the baseline in most trials but do not reach the reference on average; weaker models only tune ItemKNN. CPU time limits SASRec.
card.cheat: The hidden later days are not in the image and no test events are in the training files. Item IDs are remapped.
card.grading: NDCG@100 and Recall@100 on hidden later days with a global temporal split, normalised between the shipped ItemKNN baseline and our reference. Evaluation is deterministic code.
card.reference: Best of ItemKNN/iALS/SASRec tuned by us; paper reports ItemKNN NDCG@100 0.0934 on 50M. Closely resembles an existing ListenBrainz task, so novelty is partial.
card.source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/yandex/yambda, Apache-2.0 (card says scientific/research use only; legal check needed); paper arXiv 2505.22238
card.task: /app ships the Yambda-50M Listen+ events, the baseline ItemKNN code and an evaluator. The agent trains and tunes a recommender on CPU (ItemKNN/iALS/sequence models or popularity/recency features) and ships a model that produces top-100 lists.

source_notes: Protocol (arXiv 2505.22238v2): 300-day train window, 30-minute gap, 1-day test, users with empty history dropped, frozen model state. Natural OOD = future day(s) (temporal shift); extra shift idea: hold out last N days or cold-start users/items. Timestamps are global and binned in 5 s units. Formats: flat, multi_event, sequential parquet, plus audio embeddings (7.72M tracks). Levers: ItemKNN similarity/shrinkage, iALS regularisation and confidence, sequence models, popularity/recency features, ANN retrieval. Paper gives no hardware/training times. INFERRED: ItemKNN/iALS on 50M about 5-20 min per eval on 8 CPUs; SASRec on CPU is slow (hours). Overlap: none known.
source_version: Baseline: ItemKNN or popularity on Listen+ events, global temporal split. Paper Table 6 (Yambda-50M, Listen+): ItemKNN NDCG@100 0.0934, iALS 0.0642, SASRec 0.0764, SANSA 0.0095. -> Reference: best of ItemKNN/iALS/SASRec/SANSA, or agent-tuned model; baseline code in benchmarks/ dir of the dataset.

full_card.band: 8 h tier. Dense levers, but the tuned reference's margin over 0.0934 is unmeasured; no dated evidence for frontier success rates (E0).
full_card.build_cost: About 3-5 days: data pipeline, the GTS evaluator clone, baseline reproduction, and a reference tuned across three model families.
full_card.deliverable: A CPU recommender that outputs top-100 lists per user for hidden later days, scored by NDCG@100 and Recall@100, normalised between shipped ItemKNN and our reference.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Hidden days absent from image; offline run; item IDs remapped; evaluator and reference outside /app; reject edits to evaluator or config; no test-event leakage in training files.
full_card.grading_surface: About 10k users on hidden day(s), two metrics, deterministic evaluator; thousands of per-user scores, but one held-out day gives limited variance.
full_card.local_fit: CPU with 16 GB: 934k items x 10k users is feasible with sparse top-K ItemKNN; SASRec on CPU is slow; iALS needs careful memory; the public baseline README mentions GPU, so the CPU path must be checked.
full_card.lookup: partial: ItemKNN/iALS/SASRec baseline code is public on HF; paper gives the full protocol; the tuned reference is not public.
full_card.provenance: Yambda (Yandex) public dataset, arXiv 2505.22238 v2; Table 6 gives the 50M ItemKNN baseline NDCG@100 0.0934, and the protocol (300-day train, 30-min gap, 1-day test, frozen state) is published.
full_card.reference: Not built. Planned best-of ItemKNN (similarity, shrinkage, recency) / iALS / SASRec tuned by us; paper ItemKNN 0.0934 is the public floor.
full_card.ships: Yambda-50M listen events (flat/sequential parquet), the official ItemKNN baseline code (from the HF benchmarks folder, to be re-verified), and an evaluator; hidden later days withheld.

v1.kill_reason: Near-duplicate by cosine: S-rs-007 is another seed at 0.46, far above the 0.15 novelty threshold, and the seed says it closely resembles a ListenBrainz task. The seed-level K1 applies unless the pipeline owner confirms S-rs-007 has a different deliverable. Separately, the research-only dataset restriction needs a legal check (K6 risk, not a kill yet).

Band.why: Expected band is plausible but has no dated public evidence, so capped at 3.

Fit.why: Fits 8 CPU / 16 GB with sparse ItemKNN; SASRec on CPU is slow and the baseline README mentions GPU.

Hor.why: Sustained tuning and ensembling across several families fits 8 h.

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 metadata, but the card restricts use to scientific/research purposes; bundle shipment needs legal review.

Multi.why: Similarity, shrinkage, iALS, recency and ensembling give dense NDCG buckets.

Nov.why: Cosine 0.46 to seed S-rs-007, and the seed itself says it closely resembles a ListenBrainz task.

Real.why: Public HF dataset, arXiv paper, and official benchmark code.

Ref.why: No complete permissive reference yet; the paper baseline is a floor, not a ceiling.

Seal.why: Hidden days are withheld and the runtime is offline, but the public dataset and baseline code are readable upstream.

Surf.why: About 10k users on a hidden day with two metrics; a deterministic evaluator, but one test day is a limited surface.

spike_plan.kill_if: Baseline reproduction is off by more than 10%, the best tuned gain is under 0.005 (normalisation range too narrow), or the CPU path is infeasible.
spike_plan.pass_if: Baseline reproduces within about 5% of 0.0934, tuned ItemKNN gains at least 0.01 NDCG@100, RAM stays under 16 GB, and results are bit-identical across two runs.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, download Yambda-50M flat listens and multi_event parquet from HF (not into /app).
Rebuild the paper's GTS split: 300-day train window, 30-min gap, 1-day test, drop users with empty history, freeze state.
Run the public ItemKNN baseline (or a minimal sparse top-K cosine ItemKNN) on that split and check NDCG@100 is near 0.0934 (within about 5%).
Run a quick tuning sweep on ItemKNN (K neighbours, shrinkage, recency decay) and check the best NDCG@100 gain over 0.0934.
Time one full ItemKNN fit-and-score on 8 CPUs and record peak RAM against the 16 GB limit.
Re-run the same split twice to confirm deterministic NDCG@100.
Check whether the public benchmark code needs GPU and whether a CPU path exists.
Write the outcome and the licence question (research-only card versus bundle shipment) to the spike notes.

v1.summary: The 0.0934 ItemKNN NDCG@100 baseline and the 300-day / 30-min / 1-day GTS protocol are confirmed in the Yambda paper, and the dataset is public on HF with Apache-2.0 metadata plus a research-only restriction. The card is killed K1 because the l0 neighbour S-rs-007 is another seed at cosine 0.46, and the reference margin over the baseline is still unmeasured, so the spike must measure it.
